P0.8.title: Relay durability (D-7): file-backed store with atomic writes; a restart must lose nothing
P0.8.note: Merged as #57. Persistence is inside the mutation (on disk before put returns) and atomic (temp/fsync/rename/fsync-dir). P0.4 had TWO loss modes: the 10s timer, and writeFileSync truncating the live file so a crash mid-write lost everything rather than 10s. Failed snapshot rolls back and throws; corrupt snapshot quarantines and refuses to boot; RELAY_DUMP_PATH required unless RELAY_EPHEMERAL=1; SIGTERM handled. NOTE: the SIGKILL acceptance test first PASSED against a no-durability build because npx forks the interpreter and killing the wrapper left a grandchild on the port — now spawns the binary directly in its own process group. [E26] split to P0.9 (analysis in infra/relay/README.md), re-verified against merged M9 that the sweeper still needs seconds-precision received_at. G7's 'blocked on P0.8' dependency is now satisfied.

M11.title: UserStore round-trip (D-7 extended): the Usual and meal log cannot be read back from XTrace either; ask() is unreachable live
M11.note: SETTINGS ONLY, per D-8: the user's DECLARED facts (allergies, intolerances, budget band, portion, solo comfort, off-limits) move to a durable store; their EXPERIENCES stay in XTrace. Root cause: setUsual writes a tagged structured record, XTrace extracts it to prose, findTagged matches nothing, usual() returns null — so 'confit ask' AND 'confit confess' are both dead against live XTrace (confess reads usual() for off-limits). Probed A and B directly: 0 verbatim-JSON rows, 0 rows carrying the confit:usual tag, re-checked over 90s to rule out settle time. SAFETY, not just function: the guide's §1 says do NOT use XTrace for safety-critical facts (allergies, medical) or as a system of record, retention is ~11/16 and non-deterministic, and a dropped off-limits topic means a confession that should be blocked gets written to the pool. Recommendation: a settings namespace on the relay (atomic + fsync since P0.8). Deletes findTagged/parseTagged/newestParsed/replaceTagged/written_at ordering and the write-through cache — all of which exist only to work around the absence of addressing and upsert. Does NOT touch writeProse: that is M16/M17.

P0.9.title: Close [E26]: the relay's arrival ordering is a side channel now that it holds everything for ever
P0.9.note: Split out of P0.8, which did the durability half. D-7 makes the relay hold every read for ever rather than for minutes, so coarse timestamps move from the [prod] list to required — but neither fix fits inside infra/relay/**. (a) Coarsening received_at changes RelayEntry in src/contracts/types.ts (frozen, integrator only) AND breaks M7's sweeper, which computes a seconds-precision settle window from that exact field; M9 is rewriting the sweeper now, hence the dependency. (b) Requiring the token on GET /reads contradicts P0.4's tested 'reads stay open' and breaks M4's client, which sends no token on list(). Whoever takes this needs to decide (a) or (b) with the integrator first, because (a) is a contract change and (b) is an API change. Doing half — coarsening the field while the sweeper still needs seconds — breaks the sweeper and leaves the channel open through ?since= anyway. Analysis is written up in infra/relay/README.md under 'Known gap'.

G3 lints the catalog, which by definition does not cover text XTrace wrote. MEASURED: ingesting reads as JSON (what pool.writeRead sends today) produced the claim 'The session centers on a weekly visit to noodle_shrine that ended in regret after ordering something too spicy' — noodle_shrine, verbatim, onto a card. Run inducedClaim through K5's lint and drop it on a hit (the ask path already drops it silently on error, so the degrade path exists). Prose-rendered ingests did NOT leak an id, so M12 mitigates but does not fix this — a linter is still required because the text is not ours.

M13.title: Trust nothing about search params: the API accepts unknown fields with 200, so episode_slots may be a no-op — do the reservation client-side (R3)
M13.note: MEASURED: POST /v1/memories/search with a made-up field 'wibble_slots:99' returns 200, not 422. So sending a parameter proves NOTHING about whether it is honoured, and src/memory/client.ts:142's comment ('Explicit reservation: facts are returned before episodes') asserts a server behaviour we cannot verify. Runs with episode_slots:4, without it, and with the bogus field returned 4, 3 and 2 episodes respectively — variation that tracks non-determinism, not the parameter. The operational guide's R3 says the reservation is a CLIENT-side job and does not list episode_slots as a parameter at all. Fix: keep sending it (harmless) but implement selectTopK-style reservation in src/memory/pool.ts so the guarantee is ours. Confirmed separately: episodes DO sort after facts (first episode at index 7, consistently), so the truncation risk R3 describes is real.

M14.title: Pool ingests as prose, not JSON (guide R4) — ships WITH M12's conv_id batching; neither half works alone
M14.note: DONE with M12 in PR #60. src/memory/readProse.ts renders a read as two third-person English sentences with place NAMES; refuses to emit an id for an unknown place rather than falling back. Every possible sentence (signals x drivers x cadences) is linted by K5 in readProse.test.ts, because whatever goes into the pool can come back out onto a card. Measured effect: batching alone still leaked 3 identifier-carrying texts; batching + prose leaked 0.

M15.title: Adopting M12/M14 needs a clean pool scope: pre-M12 per-read episodes outrank the new cross-record ones
M15.note: MEASURED on the live substrate, and it is an OPERATIONAL step, not a code change. confit:pool holds episodes from both eras after M12/M14 land. The old per-read JSON ingests produced episodes like 'The session contains a single structured event rather than a back-and-forth conversation: a regret-after-order signal at Bao Bar Micro... moderate weight' — and those RANK ABOVE the new batched-prose episodes for the exact query confit ask issues. Same query against a CLEAN scope returned the real thing: a claim spanning 17 named places, no raw ids, no single-read framing. So the query was never the problem and does not need changing; the scope does. Decide with the integrator: purge confit:pool (DELETE per memory id — there is no bulk delete, see pass reset's copy) or move to a new POOL_SCOPE constant and abandon the old one. A new scope is cheaper and auditable; the old records keep costing storage quota (GET /v1/usage).

M16.title: The Ask reads all three D-8 inputs: add the PERSONAL synthesis, which is written today and never read
M16.note: D-8's missing middle. writeProse ingests every confession to the profile scope and NOTHING queries it back — grep finds no synthesis query against a profile scope anywhere, so the personal tier has been pure cost since it was written. Add UserStore.inducedClaim(profile, query) (episodes over the user's own confessions, same shape as PoolStore.inducedClaim) and thread it onto the ask path. CONTRACT CHANGE: NarratorFacts.inducedClaim is singular and would now have two callers — the personal claim ('what you keep doing') and the group claim ('what people like you keep doing') are different promises and must be separate fields, or one silently replaces the other. Also raise INDUCTION_TOP_K's lesson here: facts sort before episodes, so a profile scope thick with prose facts can push its episode past the cut — measure the index before picking k.

M17.title: Durable confession spool: verify prose is RETRIEVABLE, not merely 'complete', and re-ingest what XTrace dropped
M17.note: Under D-8 XTrace is the confession's home, which makes ~11/16 non-deterministic retention a ~30% silent loss of the user's own memory — and X2's consent copy tells them their words went to their private Confit memory. UNDETECTABLE today: verifyPendingProse clears an item when jobStatus === complete (src/memory/user.ts:258), but complete means the extraction JOB finished, not that the memory is retrievable, which is precisely the case retention drops. Guide R5 prescribes polling until retrievable and re-ingesting; that is IMPOSSIBLE in a CLI today because the pending queue is an in-process array that dies with the process (M3's own docblock) and confess exits immediately. Build a durable spool — the relay is atomic since P0.8 — holding the raw text until a SEARCH confirms XTrace has it, then delete it. A spool, NOT a second permanent copy, so the confession's home stays XTrace as D-8 requires. Guide R5 flags whether re-ingest recovers a dropped record as UNTESTED: measure it before depending on it.
